steps: Run a Python and pandas baseline exercise; note three weak areas in your weekly notes.
Use one dataset to make a data dictionary, missingness table and five exploratory plots.
Solve one SQL window question and inspect one Spark query plan.
proof: Notebook runs from the README; every field has a definition; your question and next analysis step are written.

steps: Work a small matrix multiplication and covariance example by hand.
Implement PCA with NumPy; compare components and explained variance with scikit-learn.
Review Parquet columnar storage and solve one SQL problem.
proof: Notebook explains centering, retained variance and when PCA would harm interpretation.

steps: Simulate conditional probability and Bayes rule on a small example.
Plot binomial, Poisson and normal samples; compare simulated and theoretical moments.
Diagnose one Spark join or shuffle with an execution plan.
proof: Plots have labels and a short interpretation of assumptions and uncertainty.

steps: Write a hypothesis, outcome metric, sample-size assumption and test plan.
Simulate an A/B test; calculate an interval, p-value and effect size.
Make one ingestion step safe to rerun without duplicate records.
proof: Notebook separates practical impact from statistical significance and lists bias risks.

steps: Fit a mean or majority baseline, a regularised regression and a tree model.
Compare held-out performance and inspect residuals or classification errors.
Sketch a star schema and explain the table grain.
proof: Report includes baseline, split method, metrics, assumptions and residual plots.

steps: Build a scikit-learn Pipeline for preprocessing and modelling.
Use cross-validation only on training data; keep one untouched test set.
Add a data-quality check and a short model card.
Write a one-page LLM glossary; compare zero-shot and few-shot prompts that return JSON for one data question.
proof: One command reproduces training; model card lists intended use, metrics and limits.

steps: Compare regression or logistic regression with random forest and boosting.
Inspect error slices and feature importance without claiming causality.
Review one streaming concept and solve a SQL problem.
Record ten retrieval queries and compare keyword and embedding results.
proof: Comparison table uses the same split and metric; explain where each model fails.

steps: Run clustering and PCA on a suitable dataset; check scaling and cluster stability.
Read one research paper and summarise question, method, evidence and limitations.
Record data lineage and privacy considerations for the project.
Label answers for held-out questions and calculate retrieval recall.
proof: Notebook explains why clusters are or are not useful; critique is one page.

steps: Implement a small PyTorch model with fixed seed and baseline.
Plot training and validation losses; change one hyperparameter at a time.
Review distributed loading or Parquet performance in your data pipeline.
Build a cited answerer and test at least three questions with no supporting passage.
proof: Reproducible training script, learning curves and a written failure analysis.

steps: Draw the data flow from source through quality checks to model input.
Build or refactor one batch step; test a rerun and measure runtime.
Explain a Spark join, shuffle or skew issue and one possible fix.
Score the 20-question RAG set and save failure examples.
proof: Diagram, passing checks and before/after runtime are saved with the project.

steps: Create a seasonal-naive forecast before any complex model.
Use rolling-origin backtesting and measure MAE or RMSE.
Document late data and backfill handling for the pipeline.
Test a malicious retrieved passage and document the mitigation.
proof: Forecast chart, backtest table and interval coverage or uncertainty note.

steps: Re-run one project from a clean environment.
Write README sections for question, data, methods, results, limits and reproduction.
List three specific gaps to address in weeks 13–20.
Publish the RAG baseline report with metrics, cost and latency.
proof: A reviewer can reproduce results and understand the trade-offs without asking you.

steps: Derive PCA or SVD on a small matrix and complete one MIT exercise.
Set up R and complete vector/data-frame exercises.
Check the forecasting dataset and baseline; do one SQL/Spark upkeep problem.
Save a zero-shot and few-shot prompt, their outputs and the structured-output pass rate.
proof: Saved derivation, working R script and documented forecast baseline.

steps: Work through probability or likelihood examples; run ISLP regression labs.
Use R to import, clean and summarise the forecast data.
Backtest the baseline and write what it cannot capture.
Implement one typed agent tool and test success, failure and stop paths.
proof: Lab code runs; R summary matches Python checks; baseline backtest is recorded.

steps: Simulate power and minimum detectable effect for an A/B test.
Fit a quantile forecast and compare interval coverage with the baseline.
Complete one R functions exercise and one SQL upkeep question.
Add five hard or unanswerable cases to the AI evaluation set and label failures.
proof: Notebook states metric, design assumptions, power, coverage and decision.

steps: Compare regularised, tree and boosting models on one fixed backtest.
Use R to clean missing values and produce an EDA summary.
Keep the AI work small: evaluate an existing RAG answer set.
Write a prompt-vs-RAG-vs-fine-tuning decision note for your use case.
proof: Model comparison includes error slices, runtime and a justified choice.

steps: Train a small PyTorch model; log parameters, metrics and artifacts.
Use dplyr and tidyr to reproduce one Python transformation in R.
Do one SQL/Spark upkeep problem and note the result.
Estimate token counts and cost for three representative prompts.
proof: Training can be rerun, metrics are saved, and R/Python outputs agree.

steps: Evaluate forecasting models across several time windows.
Check interval calibration and plot residuals by segment.
Make one clear ggplot2 graphic for a non-technical reader.
Test the agent tool with a denied permission, a retry and a trace.
proof: Results section reports uncertainty, failure cases and a defensible recommendation.

steps: Read two papers or technical articles; write one-page summaries with limitations.
Draft the forecasting project README and plain-English results.
For the AI project, record a small eval set and failure categories.
Run one prompt-injection test and one multimodal comparison; record results.
proof: Two cited summaries, reproducible project draft and an AI evaluation table.

steps: Run final projects from clean instructions and fix broken steps.
Publish three concise project pages or READMEs with links and screenshots.
Record remaining prerequisite gaps and the first-semester study plan.
Publish the AI demo with its evaluation set, limits and cost notes.
proof: Portfolio links work; each project shows question, method, result, limitations and your contribution.
